briefs.findings: Source inspection: ledger/__init__.py:1-3 exports Ledger. ledger/book.py:7-30 defines immutable Entry records and an in-memory ledger; post converts amounts, rejects nonpositive values and equal accounts, then appends matching debit/credit entries. Balance, statements, transfers, reversals, totals and row import/export live in the same class (32-90). Import builds entries before appending and checks their net total. ledger/_internal.py:4-5 quantizes Decimal amounts to cents. app.py:1-8 uses Ledger plus the private amount helper for an opening balance; this directly crosses the documented public-package boundary (CONTRIBUTING.md:3). startup.py:11-18 posts an opening balance, emits CSV to stdout and writes JSON to a caller-selected path. Candidate coupling: app depends on the internal conversion module; several ledger operations share posting and balance methods. This is a source dependency observation, not a measured coupling score or a reason to split the class.
